original_question: Is it true that for the Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^(2*-2)u in a general bounded domain Omega, bubble-tower sign-changing solutions in which at least two bubbles blow up at the same point on different scales can occur only in dimensions N >= 7 in the regime lambda -> 0?
target_in_paper: Section 1.3.5, Conjecture 1 (the bubble-tower conjecture for the Brezis-Nirenberg problem), rather than Open question 10: your draft asks about the λ → 0^+ threshold-dimension restriction for bubble-tower blow-up in a general domain, while Open question 10 is about fixed-parameter bubble towers in low dimensions. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2509.19863v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right PDE, the general-domain spirit, the λ → 0^+ regime, the same-point/different-scale bubble-tower profile, and the conjectured dimensional cutoff N ≥ 7. Those are exactly the ingredients surrounding the paper’s bubble-tower conjecture. ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046))
missing_details: The paper’s ambient setting is a smoothly bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ^N with N ≥ 3, not just an unspecified bounded domain. ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046))
To be stand-alone, the full Dirichlet problem should include the boundary condition u = 0 on ∂Ω. ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046))

The parameter assumptions should say λ > 0 and λ → 0^+; the draft states λ → 0 but not the positivity or one-sided limit. ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046))
The critical Sobolev exponent should be defined explicitly as 2^* = 2N/(N−2). ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046))

The conjecture is about the existence of a family/sequence of solutions exhibiting bubble-tower blow-up as λ → 0^+, not about a single isolated solution at one fixed λ. The paper separates the fixed-parameter question into Open question 10. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2509.19863v1))

Your draft adds the adjective sign-changing. That matches the nearby motivation and earlier introductory discussion, but the official conjecture itself is stated more neutrally as bubble-tower solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2509.19863v1))

Because bubble-tower is not defined in the conjecture itself, a stand-alone version should unpack it as at least two bubbles concentrating at the same point on different scales, which is the description given immediately before the conjecture. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2509.19863v1))
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^N be a smoothly bounded domain, with N ≥ 3, and consider the Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem −Δu = λu + |u|^{2^*−2}u in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, where λ > 0 and 2^* = 2N/(N−2). Is it true that if there exists a family u_λ of bubble-tower solutions as λ → 0^+—that is, solutions whose blow-up profile contains at least two bubbles concentrating at the same point on different scales—then necessarily N ≥ 7? ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046))
justification: This is the nearest official target because Section 1.3.5 states precisely that, in a general bounded domain Ω, bubble-tower solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem can only exist for N ≥ 7 as λ → 0, and the immediately preceding sentence identifies the motivating low-dimensional obstruction as the nonexistence of configurations with two bubbles blowing up at the same point. The earlier introduction also frames the known constructions in this direction as sign-changing bubble towers. So your draft is aimed at the right conjectural threshold question, but it needs the full problem data and slightly more neutral wording to match the paper exactly. Page numbers are unavailable in the published version because the AIMS article is still Early Access and explicitly notes that no page numbers have yet been assigned. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2509.19863v1))
